o1.biggest_strength: It pins everything to the winning segment and trigger, and keeps the forecast honest by refusing to multiply two gains the pilot never tested together (6.8% floor, 7.9% trigger, plan on ~7%), with list rules that also rest the 1,300 pilot contacts and exclude the 4,100 wrong-fit names.
o1.biggest_mistake: Several emails carry a question plus a second conditional ask ("reply 'yes'", "reply 'steps'") and promise two assets that don't exist yet, so the one-question-one-ask rule and the ready-to-send claim both slip.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make one open question the only call to action in every email, with the one-page summary and three-step write-up already drafted, and show the forecast both per 100 and across the full 1,900.

o2.biggest_strength: It shows its funnel math openly (half of Controllers' replies turned positive, 86% of those booked) and delivers four clean, link-free, spec-compliant emails with the decision stated in one line.
o2.biggest_mistake: It forecasts ~8% with a 10% ceiling built on an invented "role adds a quarter on top of the trigger" multiplier, so the headline number is the wish the owner explicitly warned against even though the pilot never tested segment and trigger together.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Replace the 1.25 uplift with the pilot-backed 6.8-7.9% band as the expectation and add list hygiene for the 1,300 Controllers who already received the old sequence.

reason: Both write the right sequence for the right people, but Output 1's forecast is the one I could defend to my board (it refuses to stack untested gains and maps cleanly to ~130 replies from 1,900), while Output 2's 8%-to-10% range rests on a made-up uplift. Output 1 also handles list overlap with the pilot, which Output 2 ignores.
